**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), fallback-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations inspected:** § 20(d) (p0142, general assignment clause), § 3(c) (p0033, Customer-only assignment/transfer prohibition), § 17 term/termination (p0116–p0122), § 2 grant (p0028). A full-document search for "change of control" returned nothing, so Garman has no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right — no element gap there and nothing to delete.
- **Why it fails fallback:** § 20(d) requires consent for every assignment with no successor carve-out, no written-notice mechanic and no reasonableness standard; § 3(c) additionally imposes a one-sided blanket bar on Sparkling assigning the Agreement absent Garman's written authorisation.
- **Cure (2 surgical ops):** § 20(d) rewritten to mutual successor assignment on written notice with consent for other assignments not to be unreasonably withheld; the words "assign this Agreement or" struck from § 3(c) so the retained Work-transfer restrictions survive verbatim but no longer contradict the new clause. No affiliate no-consent exception was added, since that would conflict with the fallback's "other assignments require consent."
